cues.en: Every day we engage in a behavior that is completely contrary to how we would optimally function. And I'm not talking about a modern technological practice such as posting embarrassing snapshots of one's unsuspecting partner on Facebook. I'm talking about an integral human behavior. I'm talking about a deeply intimate behavior. Every day we engage in a behavior that requires us to distort our thoughts
cues.zh: 我们每天都在做着一种完全违背人类最佳运行状态的行为。我说的并不是什么现代科技产物，比如在 Facebook 上发伴侣毫无防备的尴尬抓拍。我说的是一种不可或缺的人类行为，一种极其私密的行为。我们每天都在做的这种行为，不仅需要我们扭曲思想、

cues.en: numb our feelings, and act against our core values, and which enables a global atrocity that can make even the most stoic of us weep in sorrow. And every day we could choose not to engage in this behavior, except we don't realize that it's irrational, we don't see that it's destructive, and we don't even know we have a choice. How can some of the most
cues.zh: 麻木情感，违背自身的核心价值观，而且还助长了一场足以让最坚强的人都悲伤落泪的全球暴行。每一天，我们本可以选择不做这件事，但我们却没有意识到它的荒谬，看不到它的破坏性，甚至根本不知道自己还有得选。为什么我们做出的一些最

cues.en: frequent and important choices we make appear not to be choices at all. How can the irrationality and destruction of a widespread behavior be virtually invisible? These are the questions I asked when I began my nearly two decades of research on the psychology of eating animals. And what I discovered was not at all what I had expected.
cues.zh: 频繁、最重要的抉择，看起来却根本不算是一种选择？一种普遍行为的荒谬与破坏性，究竟是如何变得几乎隐形不可见的？这些正是近二十年前，我着手研究食用动物的心理学时所提出的问题。而我的发现，完全出乎了我的意料。

cues.en: As it turns out, there is a distinct underlying factor that both drives our behavior and prevents us from recognizing its irrationality and the destruction it causes. I identified and codified this factor, and I'm here to share my findings with you. And the good news is that simply becoming aware of this factor enables us to reclaim our rationality and freedom of choice, and to become more active participants in creating a humane and just world.
cues.zh: 事实证明，存在着一个明确的潜在因素，它既驱动着我们的行为，又阻止我们认清其荒谬性与带来的破坏。我确定并总结了这个因素，今天就来和大家分享我的研究发现。好消息是，只要意识到这个因素的存在，我们就能找回理智与选择的自由，并能更积极地参与建设一个充满人道与公正的世界。

cues.en: My journey of discovery began in 1968, 25 years before I set foot in my first Harvard lecture, and nearly 50 years before I received the Ahimsa Award at the British House of Commons for my work on global nonviolence. I'm 48, so thank you. My family adopted a puppy we named Fritz. Now Fritz was my first dog, and he was also my first friend.
cues.zh: 我的探索之旅始于1968年，那是在我初次踏入 Harvard 课堂的25年前，也是因在全球非暴力领域的工作而在英国下议院荣获 Ahimsa Award 的近50年前。我今年48岁，谢谢大家。当时我们家收养了一只小狗，取名叫 Fritz。Fritz 是我的第一只狗，也是我的第一个朋友。

cues.en: We did everything together. We played together, we napped together, and we even vomited together once during a sickening road trip. And Fritz was also my first heartbreak when he died at the age of 13 of liver cancer. What I didn't realize back then was that my connection with Fritz would lead to a discovery that would transform my world view. So I cared about Fritz.
cues.zh: 我们形影不离。一起玩耍，一起打盹，甚至有一次在让人反胃的公路旅行中一起吐得稀里哗啦。13岁那年，Fritz 因肝癌去世，那也是我人生中第一次体验心碎。当时我并未意识到，我和 Fritz 之间的羁绊，竟会引出一项彻底改变我世界观的发现。我深深在乎 Fritz。

cues.en: And I'm not unique. Most of us care about animals. We teach our children to be kind to animals. Our hearts leap when we witness them at play. We recognize the injustice and feel outraged when they are abused. We empathize with animals. We share their fear, their joy, their sorrow. And how many of you have cared about a certain animal in your life? Just raise your hand. Now look around the room.
cues.zh: 而我并非特例。我们大多数人都在乎动物。我们教导孩子要善待动物。看到它们嬉戏玩闹，我们的心也会雀跃。当看到它们遭受虐待时，我们会认清这种不公并感到义愤填膺。我们对动物感同身受。我们体会它们的恐惧、它们的喜悦、它们的悲伤。在座的各位，有谁生命中曾在乎过某只动物吗？请举一下手。现在，请看看周围的人。

cues.en: That's a whole lot of caring. So to explain how my connection with my dog led me to this stage, I'd like to do a thought experiment. Imagine that you're a guest at a dinner party, and your host serves you a dish that looks like this. Consider whether you'd find this delicious or disgusting. For those who would find it delicious, imagine you find it so delicious that you ask your host for the recipe. And she replies that the secret is in the meat.
cues.zh: 这真是满满的关怀。为了解释我与狗的联结如何把我带到这个舞台，我想做个思想实验。想象你是晚宴上的客人，主人给你端上一道看起来这样的菜。想一想，你会觉得它美味还是恶心。觉得美味的人，再想象你觉得它太好吃了，于是向主人要食谱。她回答你，秘诀在肉里。

cues.en: You use three pounds of well-seasoned Golden Retriever. Now take a moment to reflect on your thoughts and feelings. Chances are what you had just thought of as food, you now think of as a dead animal. What you just felt was delicious, you now feel is disgusting. Chances are your experience of the meat dramatically changed, even though nothing about the meat itself actually changed. So what changed?
cues.zh: 你用三磅调味好的金毛寻回犬。现在花点时间体会一下自己的想法和感受。很可能，你刚才还当作食物的东西，现在会想成一只死去的动物。你刚才觉得美味的东西，现在觉得恶心。很可能你对这块肉的体验彻底变了，尽管肉本身其实没有任何变化。那么，变的是什么？

cues.en: Well, what changed is your perception of the meat. And when it comes to eating animals, our perception is shaped largely, if not entirely, by our culture. In meat-eating cultures around the world, out of over 7 million animal species, people tend to classify only a handful as edible. All the rest are inedible and disgusting.
cues.zh: 变的是你对这块肉的认知。说到吃动物，我们的认知很大程度上——甚至完全——由文化塑造。在世界各地的肉食文化中，超过700万种动物里，人们往往只把少数几种归为可食用。其余的都是不可食用、令人恶心的。

cues.en: So the question is, why are we not disgusted by the select species we have learned to think of as edible? And why don't we ever ask why? Have you ever wondered why you might eat certain animals but not others? Have you ever wondered why you haven't wondered? For much of my life, I never wondered about my choice to eat certain animals because I never even knew I had a choice.
cues.zh: 所以问题是，为什么我们不会对被我们学会当作可食用的那几种动物感到恶心？为什么我们从来不问为什么？你有没有想过，为什么你会吃某些动物却不吃另一些？你有没有想过，为什么自己从没想过？在我人生的大部分时间里，我从未想过自己吃某些动物的选择，因为我甚至不知道我有选择。

cues.en: No one had ever asked me if I believed in eating animals. Eating animals was just a given. So I never thought about how strange it was that I could pet my dog with one hand while I ate a pork chop with the other. A pork chop that had once been an animal who was at least as sentient and intelligent as my dog. And frankly, I didn't want to think about this contradiction. It was just easier not to.
cues.zh: 从来没人问过我，我是否认同吃动物。吃动物只是理所当然的事。所以我从没想过，这有多奇怪：我可以一只手抚摸我的狗，另一只手吃着猪排。而那块猪排曾经是一只动物，它的感受能力和智力至少和我的狗一样。说实话，我不想去想这个矛盾。不去想，总是更容易。

cues.en: It wasn't until 1989 that I started asking why. I had been hospitalized after eating what would be my very last hamburger, a burger that was contaminated with the dangerous bacteria campylobacter. After being so sick, I swore off meat, and then something interesting happened. When I stopped eating animals, I had a paradigm shift. In other words,
cues.zh: 直到1989年，我才开始问为什么。我吃了后来成为我最后一个汉堡的汉堡后住了院，那个汉堡被危险的弯曲杆菌污染了。病得那么重之后，我发誓不再吃肉，然后有趣的事情发生了。当我停止吃动物后，我经历了一次范式转变。换句话说，

cues.en: I didn't see different things. I saw the same things differently. Beef stew seemed no different than golden retriever stew. And everywhere I turned, I saw people putting the bodies of dead animals into their mouths as though nothing at all were wrong. So I became very curious as to how rational, caring people, like myself, could just stop thinking and feeling. Well, two advanced degrees later,
cues.zh: 我看到的不是不同的东西。我是用不同的方式看同样的东西。炖牛肉看起来和炖金毛寻回犬没什么不同。无论我转向哪里，我都看到人们把死去动物的尸体放进嘴里，仿佛一切都没有问题。于是我变得非常好奇：像我自己这样理性、有爱心的人，怎么能就这样停止思考和感受。后来，又拿了两个高级学位，

cues.en: I had my answer. And this is what I discovered. There is an invisible belief system or ideology that conditions us to eat certain animals. And I named the system Carnism. We tend to assume that only vegans and vegetarians follow a belief system, but when eating animals is not a necessity, which is the case in much of the world today, then it is a choice.
cues.zh: 我有了答案。而这是我发现的。存在一套无形的信念体系或意识形态，训练我们去吃某些动物。我把这套体系命名为Carnism。我们往往以为只有纯素食者和素食者才遵循一套信念体系，但当吃动物并非必要时——在当今世界许多地方都是如此——那它就是一种选择。

cues.en: and choices always stem from beliefs. Now, carnism is a dominant ideology, meaning that it's so widespread, its doctrine is seen as a given rather than a choice. Eating animals is just the way things are. And it is a violent ideology. Meat cannot be procured without violence, and egg and dairy production cause extensive harm to animals.
cues.zh: 而选择总是源于信念。肉食主义是一种主导意识形态，这意味着它极其普遍，其信条被视为理所当然，而非一种选择。吃肉不过是顺理成章的事。而且这是一种暴力的意识形态。肉类不可能脱离暴力而获得，蛋奶生产也对动物造成了巨大的伤害。

cues.en: Ideologies such as carnism run counter to core human values. Values such as compassion, justice, and authenticity. And so they need to use defense mechanisms that distort our thoughts and numb our feelings so that we act against our values without fully realizing what we are doing. Now the main defense of carnism is denial, which is expressed largely through invisibility.
cues.zh: 像肉食主义这样的意识形态违背了人类的核心价值观。比如同情、正义和真诚。因此它们必须利用防御机制来扭曲我们的思想，麻痹我们的感受，让我们在没有完全意识到自己在做什么的情况下，做出违背自身价值观的行为。肉食主义最主要的防御机制就是否认，而这主要通过隐形化来体现。

cues.en: The ideology itself is invisible, and so are its victims. For instance, 1.2 billion farmed animals are slaughtered globally every week. So in one week, more farmed animals are killed than the total number of people killed in all wars throughout history. But how many of these animals have you seen? So where are they?
cues.zh: 这种意识形态本身是隐形的，它的受害者同样也是隐形的。例如，全球每周有12亿只养殖动物被屠杀。仅仅一周内被杀害的养殖动物，就超过了有史以来所有战争中死亡人数的总和。但你亲眼见过其中的多少只呢？那么它们都在哪里？

cues.en: Approximately 98% of the meat, eggs, and dairy we eat comes from animals who were raised in factory farms or windowless sheds in remote locations that are virtually impossible to obtain access to. Yet, although these animals are treated as commodities, they are in fact sentient, intelligent individuals with lives that matter to them.
cues.zh: 我们食用的肉类、蛋类和奶制品中，约有98%来自工厂化农场或偏远地区无窗棚舍中饲养的动物，那些地方几乎无法进入。然而，尽管这些动物被当作商品对待，但它们实际上是有感知、有智慧的生命个体，拥有对它们自身至关重要的生命。

cues.en: Now, in a moment, I'm going to show a two-minute video of animal factories, which can be difficult to watch. So I want to remind you that my intention is simply to raise awareness. So I have to make the invisible visible. I select a material that I think is sufficient to inform you without traumatizing you. But if it's too difficult to watch, just close your eyes and plug your ears. Piglets are castrated by workers who cut into their skin.
cues.zh: 稍后，我将播放一段两分钟关于动物工厂的视频，可能会让人感到不适。所以我想提醒大家，我的目的只是为了唤起人们的意识。为此，我必须让看不见的事实显现出来。我选取的素材既能足以告知大家真相，又不至于造成心理创伤。但如果觉得难以承受，闭上眼睛、捂住耳朵即可。工人们切开小猪的皮肤对其进行阉割。

cues.en: and rip out their testicles. Next, the workers chop off their tails. Once pigs have reached market weight, they are sent to slaughter. At the slaughterhouse, pigs are knocked in the head with a steel rod, hung upside down, and have their throats slit. One proper stunning condemns many pigs to having their throats slit while they are fully conscious and suffering. Because male chicks don't lay eggs and do not grow quickly enough to be raised profitably for meat, they are killed within hours after hatching.
cues.zh: 并扯出它们的睾丸。接着，工人们砍掉它们的尾巴。一旦猪长到出栏体重，就会被送去屠宰。在屠宰场，猪的头部会被钢棒击打，倒挂起来，然后被割断喉咙。致昏不当导致许多猪在完全清醒、痛苦万分的情况下被割喉。因为公雏鸡不下蛋，而且生长速度不够快、无法用于肉类养殖盈利，它们在孵化后几小时内就会被处死。

cues.en: The females have it even worse. Workers use a hot blade or laser to remove part of the chick's beaks. At the slaughter plant, the birds are dumped from their crates, then roughly snapped upside down into moving shackles by their fragile legs. They are then pulled across a blade which slices their throats, causing blood to pour from their necks. Calves on dairy farms are dragged away from their mothers and violently killed.
cues.zh: 母雏鸡的遭遇甚至更糟。工人们用热刀片或激光切掉雏鸡的一部分喙。在屠宰厂，这些禽类被从箱子里倒出来，然后脆弱的双腿被粗暴地倒挂在移动的铁钩上。接着它们被拖过刀片割断喉咙，鲜血从脖颈处喷涌而出。奶牛场的小牛则被强行从母亲身边拖走并残忍杀害。

cues.en: The majority of today's dairy cows are confined on factory farms. Workers subject young cows to painful mutilations and amputations. Unreliable, stunning practices at the slaughterhouse condemn many cattle to having their throats cut and their limbs hacked off while still alive and conscious. Massive, trawling nets indiscriminately drag hundreds of tons of fish and other animals along the ocean floor.
cues.zh: 今天大多数奶牛被关在工厂化农场里。工人会让小牛遭受痛苦的残割和截肢。屠宰场不可靠的致昏操作，使许多牛在仍然活着且有意识时被割喉、砍断四肢。巨大的拖网不分青红皂白地沿海底拖拽数百吨鱼和其他动物。

cues.en: They are then tossed on board where the surviving fish either suffocate or are crushed to death. Thank you. I know it can be painful to see that. Fortunately for us, the hard part's over. But before we move on, I want to just point out that this footage focuses on standard industry practices, including in so-called humane or bio facilities. And I also want to point out that there is a gift in our pain.
cues.zh: 然后它们被扔到船上，活下来的鱼要么窒息，要么被压死。谢谢。我知道看到这些可能很难受。对我们来说幸运的是，最难的部分已经过去了。但在继续之前，我想指出，这段影像聚焦的是行业标准做法，包括在所谓人道或生物设施中的做法。我还想指出，我们的痛苦中也有一份礼物。

cues.en: Our pain is the mirror in which we can see the reflection of our humanity. So, clearly, the animals pay for our carnism, but we are also victims of the system. We pay for our carnism with our health, as eating an animal-based diet can lead to serious disease, while eating a plant-based or vegan diet can optimize health. And we pay for our carnism with our hearts and with our minds, with our...
cues.zh: 我们的痛苦是一面镜子，在其中能看到我们人性的映照。所以很明显，动物为我们的肉食主义付出代价，但我们也是这个体系的受害者。我们用自己的健康为肉食主义付出代价，因为以动物性食物为主的饮食会导致严重疾病，而植物性饮食或纯素饮食可以改善健康。我们还用自己的心和头脑为肉食主义付出代价，用我们被削弱的同理心，以及被削弱的客观性。

cues.en: dampened empathy, and diminished objectivity. But of course, invisibility alone cannot maintain the system. Hints of the truth surround us. So another defense is necessary, justification. And the way that we learn to justify eating animals is by learning to believe that the myths of meat, eggs, and dairy are the facts of meat, eggs, and dairy. These myths are expressed largely through what I refer to as the three ends of justification.
cues.zh: 但当然，仅靠不可见性无法维持这个体系。真相的暗示环绕着我们。所以还需要另一种防御：合理化。我们学会为吃动物辩护的方式，就是学会相信关于肉、蛋、奶的神话就是肉、蛋、奶的事实。这些神话主要通过我所说的“合理化的三大目的”表达出来。

cues.en: Eating animals is, what do you think? You're good, fat, great. Okay, normal, natural, and necessary. And haven't we heard this somewhere before? Slavery is normal, natural, and necessary. Male dominance is normal, natural, and necessary. Heterosexual supremacy is normal, natural, and necessary.
cues.zh: 吃动物是——你们觉得呢？你们很好，太棒了。好，正常、自然、必要。我们以前难道没听过这套说法吗？奴隶制是正常、自然、必要的。男性支配是正常、自然、必要的。异性恋至上主义是正常、自然、必要的。

cues.en: And as with other dominant violent ideologies, the myths of carnism are institutionalized. So, carnistic bias is embedded within the very foundations of the system. And when we are born into an institutionalized system such as carnism, we inevitably internalize it. We learn to look at the world through the lens of carnism. And carnism uses a set of defenses that distort our perceptions of farmed animals.
cues.zh: 和其他占主导地位的暴力意识形态一样，肉食主义的神话也被制度化了。因此，肉食主义偏见嵌入了这个体系的最基础层面。当我们出生在像肉食主义这样被制度化的体系中，我们不可避免地会将其内化。我们学会透过肉食主义的透镜看世界。而肉食主义使用一套防御机制，扭曲我们对养殖动物的认知。

cues.en: For instance, carnism teaches us to see farmed animals as abstractions, as lacking any individuality or personality of their own. A pig is a pig, and all pigs are the same. And carnism blinds us to the absurdities of the system. Voltaire was right. If we believe absurdities, we shall commit atrocities.
cues.zh: 例如，肉食主义教我们把养殖动物看作抽象概念，认为它们缺乏自己的个体性或个性。猪就是猪，所有猪都一样。肉食主义还让我们看不到这个体系的荒诞之处。伏尔泰说得对。如果我们相信荒诞之事，就会犯下暴行。

cues.en: And Carnism is but one of the many atrocities, one of the many violent ideologies that are an unfortunate part of the human legacy. And although the experience of each set of victims will always be somewhat unique, the ideologies themselves are similar. The mentality that enables such violence is the same. It's the mentality of domination and subjugation, of privilege and oppression.
cues.zh: 而肉食主义只是人类历史上众多暴行、众多暴力意识形态之一，是不幸遗产的一部分。尽管每群受害者的经历总有其独特性，但这些意识形态本身是相似的。促成这种暴力的心态是相同的。那就是支配与征服、特权与压迫的心态。

cues.en: It's the mentality that causes us to turn someone into something, to reduce a life to a unit of production. It is the might-makes-right mentality that makes us feel entitled to wield complete control over the lives and deaths of those with less power, just because we can, and to feel justified in our actions because they're only savages, women, animals.
cues.zh: 正是这种心态让我们把“某个生命”当成“某样东西”，把一条生命贬低为一个生产单元。正是这种“强权即公理”的心态，让我们觉得自己有权对弱者的生死拥有绝对控制，仅仅因为我们做得到；并让我们觉得自己的行为理所应当，因为他们“只不过”是野蛮人、女性、动物。

cues.en: It is the mentality of meat. And so if we fail to pick out the common threads that are woven through all violent ideologies, then we will recreate atrocities in new forms. But if we identify these common threads, then we can unravel atrocities in all forms. And so this brings us to our final question. What is the solution?
cues.zh: 这就是肉食的心态。所以，如果我们未能找出贯穿所有暴力意识形态的共同线索，就会以新的形式重蹈覆辙。但如果我们认清了这些共同线索，就能瓦解各种形式的暴行。这就引出了我们最后一个问题：解决之道是什么？

cues.en: How can we lead more authentic and freely chosen lives and bring our optimal selves into the world? Well, it turns out the solution is already in our grasp. 17 minutes ago, you may not have been aware of carnism, the invisible ideology that disconnects us from our rationality, our feelings, and our values, and which enables a massive global injustice. You couldn't see carnism. Now, you can. Now, you are aware.
cues.zh: 我们怎样才能过上更真实、更自主选择的生活，把最好的自己带给这个世界？其实，答案早已在我们手中。17分钟前，你可能还不知道肉食主义——这种无形的意识形态切断了我们与理性、情感和价值观的联系，并促成了席卷全球的巨大不公。那时你看不见肉食主义。现在，你看到了。现在，你已经意识到了。

cues.en: Your awareness is the first step of the solution. And acting from your awareness is the rest. And awareness has always been the antidote to violent ideologies. Virtually every atrocity was made possible because the populace turned away from a reality they felt was too painful to face.
cues.zh: 你的觉醒就是解决方案的第一步。而顺应这份觉醒去行动，则是接下来的全部。觉醒一直是对抗暴力意识形态的解药。几乎每一场暴行的发生，都是因为大众逃避了他们觉得痛苦到无法直视的现实。

cues.en: And virtually every revolution, every social transformation was made possible because of those who chose awareness and who acted on what they had learned. And the good news is that there is an alternative to carnism. The vegan movement, which is the counterpoint to carnism, is one of the fastest growing social justice movements in the world today. And the good news is also that we can make minor changes that will have a major impact.
cues.zh: 而几乎每一场变革、每一次社会转型，都是因为有人选择了觉醒，并根据所认清的现实采取了行动。好消息是，肉食主义是有替代方案的。作为肉食主义对立面的纯素主义运动，是当今世界上发展最快的社会正义运动之一。另一个好消息是，我们只需做出微小的改变，就能产生巨大的影响。

cues.en: We can reduce and ultimately eliminate our consumption of meat, eggs, and dairy. To start, we can eat just one vegan meal a day or one vegan day a week, and we can spread Carnism Awareness, which is the mission of my organization, Beyond Carnism. It's simple. If each of us shares this talk with everyone we know, and they do the same, Carnism Awareness will inevitably reach critical mass,
cues.zh: 我们可以减少并最终杜绝肉、蛋、奶的消费。刚开始，我们可以每天吃一顿纯素餐，或者每周吃一天纯素；我们还可以传播“肉食主义意识”，这也是我创办的机构 Beyond Carnism 的使命。其实很简单。如果大家把这个演讲分享给认识的每个人，他们也照做，肉食主义意识就必然会达到临界规模，

cues.en: and will bring about a global paradigm shift. So, we have the potential to change the world if you believe that carnism awareness is an idea worth spreading. Thank you.
cues.zh: 并带来一场全球性的观念转变。所以，只要你相信“肉食主义意识”是一个值得传播的理念，我们就有潜力改变世界。谢谢大家。
